title: A finite symmetric-product cover over a Noetherian base
statement:
For a Noetherian scheme $S$ and $n\geq1$, the
symmetric-product map
$\sigma_n:(\mathbf P^1_S)^n\to\mathbf P^n_S$ is finite and surjective,
in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions].

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-finite] to the given scheme $S$ and integer $n\ge1$. Its morphism uses exactly the coefficients $\prod_i(x_it+y_i)=\sum_{j=0}^nF_jt^j$ and the construction of [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-properties], so it is the $\sigma_n$ of this statement. The lemma gives that $\sigma_n$ is finite. Its hypothesis is only that $S$ is a scheme; the present Noetherian hypothesis is therefore more than sufficient.

source.place: Tag 0A4F, label lemma-reduce-to-P1, proof, final paragraph (finite surjective symmetric-product morphism; coefficient order reversed)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-surjective] with the same $S$ and $n$. The coefficient formula and the constructed morphism in its statement are identical to those in the finiteness lemma, so its conclusion says that this same $\sigma_n$ is surjective on underlying topological spaces. Together with step 1 this gives both assertions, with the meanings fixed by the conventions in the statement.
